subject: Northbridge / Redwood connector: reference scenarios & performance probe
messages:
From: David Li <david.li@northbridge.io>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Northbridge / Redwood connector: reference scenarios & performance probe

Hi Connor / Laura —

Thanks again for taking time last week. As discussed, we want to validate the connector behavior with a small set of realistic production scenarios before committing to the dedicated bundle. Attached are: connector-spec-v1.pdf (interface + auth details), sample-load.csv (representative requests), and a short log excerpt showing the current request patterns.

Top asks from our side:
- Can Redwood support the multi-tenant prefix caching scheme in section 3 of the spec? We currently use a tenant->session map that expects sticky routing.
- We need to validate tail latency at 99th pct for 1–2k concurrent streams (see sample-load).
- What are the recommended quantization / model variants for lower-cost fallback during high burst windows?

Proposed run: lightweight compatibility run using a Redwood hosted test model, then a short on-prem smoke if the hosted pass is green. Goal: go/no-go by end of next week.

Attachment stubs: [Attachment: connector-spec-v1.pdf (PDF)], [Attachment: sample-load.csv (CSV)], [Attachment: nbridge-api-logs-08-31.txt (TXT)]

Quick note on compliance — procurement will ask for SOC2 pointer; I included procurement@northbridge.io on copy for later.

Thanks,
David
David Li
Head of Platform Partnerships
Northbridge Technologies


From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Li <david.li@northbridge.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Northbridge / Redwood connector: reference scenarios & performance probe

David —

Appreciate the materials, this is exactly the level of detail we need. High level answers up front:
- Multi-tenant prefix caching: we can support the pattern, but we need to lock down the exact eviction and KV sizing expectations. Our runtime exposes tenant-aware KV namespaces; the main question is expected cache hit ratio in your workloads.
- 99th pct tail latency for 1–2k streams: doable on Dedicated with our burst profile, and we can simulate this on hosted using a scaled load harness. We’ll provide a latency baseline report.
- Quantization fallback: recommend a 4-bit quantized variant for cost-sensitive fallbacks; we can provide a quality delta report against your prompty set.

Next steps I propose (action items):
1) Connor to run a hosted compatibility pass using the sample-load and your auth test keys — target Thursday 9/16.
2) Laura to schedule a short joint smoke test plan and confirm resource window for a Dedicated burst test (possible Friday 9/17).
3) Kimberly to pull SOC2 / compliance pointer and send the cert link to procurement.

Laura / Kimberly — assigning to you for scheduling and compliance artifacts. Dave — expect a short readout from us after the hosted run; if green we’ll propose a half-day engaged smoke on your Dedicated environment.

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: run-plan-template.md (MD)]


From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Li <david.li@northbridge.io>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Northbridge / Redwood connector: reference scenarios & performance probe

David —

We ran the hosted compatibility pass this morning against your sample-load and the connector spec. Summary:
- Functional: auth flows and tenant prefix behavior validated for the sample set. Two minor token refresh edge cases noted (see readout below).
- Performance: 95th latency at baseline is within expectations; 99th for the 1k simulated streams shows a 450ms tail on hosted test model. Based on our Dedicated profiles we expect the 99th to drop to ~220–280ms with the right pool size and prewarmed KV shards.
- Quality: fallback quantized variant (4-bit) introduces average 3.7% perplexity increase on your prompt set; we recommend using it only for emergency fallback and not for primary path.

Readout (short):
* Token refresh edge: when session duration < 30s and burst > 10 rps per session we saw intermittent 401s. Mitigation: increase refresh window or centralize refresh from gateway.
* Cache sizing: for projected tenant set we estimate 24GB effective KV per shard; will provide a sizing spreadsheet.

Action items completed: hosted pass (Connor), SOC2 pointer attached by Kimberly (link below).

Next: we propose a dedicated half-day smoke on Monday 9/20 09:00–13:00 PT to validate the tail latency under a realistic network topology. If that window works for you, we’ll lock it and share runbook + run-play artifacts.

Links / attachments: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2BnbNorthbridgeSpec (readout doc), HUBSPOT-Contact-378412

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
